theme: ज्ञान-उत्थान और योग-स्थित जीवन | Knowledge, clarity, and yoga-anchored action
context: Krishna has been explaining that true wisdom is not passivity but action without egoic attachment. Arjuna is still in moral and emotional conflict, but the Lord shifts the focus from outward duty to inward freedom: one who has cut doubt through knowledge and remains rooted in the Self is no longer bound by action.
contextHindi: श्रीकृष्ण ने समझाया है कि सच्चा ज्ञान निष्क्रियता नहीं, अहंकाररहित कर्म है। अर्जुन अभी नैतिक और भावनात्मक द्वन्द्व में है, पर भगवान ने बात को बाहर के कर्तव्य से भीतर की मुक्ति की ओर मोड़ दिया है: जो व्यक्ति ज्ञान से संशय को काट देता है और आत्मा में स्थिर रहता है, वह कर्म से नहीं बंधता।
sanskritDevanagari:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् |
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ||४-४१||
transliteration:
yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasañchinnasaṃśayam .
ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya ||4-41||

wordByWord.meaning: one whose actions are renounced through yoga; action is no longer driven by ego and attachment.
whose doubts are cut asunder by knowledge; inner uncertainty has been resolved.
self-possessed, rooted in the Self, inwardly established.
do not bind; they do not create karmic entanglement.

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक कहता है कि योग में स्थित व्यक्ति कर्म करता हुआ भी कर्मों से बंधता नहीं। ‘योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणम्’ का अर्थ है वह, जिसने योग के द्वारा कर्मों का संन्यास किया है। इसका मतलब काम छोड़ देना नहीं, बल्कि कर्म को बंधन बनाने वाली आसक्ति से मुक्त होना है। ‘ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम्’ उस व्यक्ति को कहता है जिसके संशय ज्ञान से कट गए हैं। ‘आत्मवन्तम्’ का अर्थ है आत्मसंयमी और आत्मा में स्थित। ऐसे व्यक्ति को कर्म बांधते नहीं, हे धनंजय। यहाँ कर्म का परिणाम मिट जाने की बात नहीं है; श्लोक कहता है कि कर्म उस व्यक्ति को बंधन में नहीं डालते। पिछले श्लोकों में कृष्ण ने ज्ञान और योग से कर्म के बंधन से मुक्त होने की बात कही है। इस श्लोक में वे बताते हैं कि ज्ञान से संशय दूर हो और व्यक्ति आत्मसंयम में स्थित हो, तो कर्म करते हुए भी बंधन नहीं रहता।
clearEnglish: This verse is not a call to spiritual laziness. It is the description of a person whose inner center has changed. “Yogasaṃnyasta-karmāṇam” means one who has renounced action in the yogic sense: not abandoning duty in the outer world, but letting go of the egoic idea that “I am the doer.” “Jñānasañchinna-saṃśayam” means the person whose doubts have been cut through by knowledge. Such a person is no longer trapped by the compulsions of action. The verse is careful: it does not deny the world of karma; it denies the binding power of karma when the self is no longer identified with the doer. In ordinary life, we often act from fear, pride, comparison, or reward-seeking. In the yogic state, action continues, but it is transformed. The verse therefore describes inner freedom as a shift in identity, not a withdrawal from responsibility. It is psychologically honest: clarity reduces compulsive reactivity.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states the condition: one who has renounced actions by yoga, whose doubts are cut by knowledge, and who is self-possessed is not bound by actions. The emphasis is on the change in inner attitude rather than on abandoning all action.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A reasonable conclusion is that ethical action can become liberating when it is no longer driven by ego, craving, or fear. The inner state matters as much as the outer act; action becomes a channel of clarity rather than a chain of bondage.

practicalApplication.label: Pause before action
practicalApplication.text: Before speaking or deciding, ask: 'Am I acting from ego, fear, or reward? Or from clarity and responsibility?' This simple pause reduces impulsive choices.

practicalApplication.label: Observe the doer
practicalApplication.text: Notice the moment when the thought 'I must do this' becomes 'I am choosing what is needed.' That shift often reduces tension and helps action become more balanced.

reflectionQuestion: When have you acted most freely: when you were trying to control the outcome, or when you were clear about your duty without clinging to the result?
reflectionQuestionHindi: आपने कब सबसे अधिक स्वतंत्रता महसूस की—जब आप परिणाम को नियंत्रित करने की कोशिश कर रहे थे, या जब आप बिना परिणाम से चिपके अपने कर्तव्य के प्रति स्पष्ट थे?
